text.p: Lens maker Essilor said on Monday sales rose 22 percent in the first five months of the year, helped by acquisitions and foreign exchange movements, but turnover rose less than expected on a like-for-like basis.

"In the first five months of the year, growth was 22 percent, with 14 percent coming from changes in structure and five percent from currency changes," chairman Xavier Fontanet told the annual general meeting.

Stripping out the benefits of changes in structure and exchange rates, the sales rise was three percent, "lower than our expectations", he said. Sales in Germany and northern Europe were showing very weak improvement, he said.
